paragraphs: We are a transportation and logistics company engaged primarily in transporting truckload shipments of general commodities in both interstate and intrastate commerce. We also provide logistics services through our Werner Logistics segment. We believe we are one of the largest truckload carriers in the United States (based on total operating revenues), and our headquarters are located in Omaha, Nebraska, near the geographic center of our truckload service area. We were founded in 1956 by Clarence L. Werner, who started the business with one truck at the age of 19. We were incorporated in the State of Nebraska in September 1982 and completed our initial public offering in June 1986 with a fleet of 632 trucks as of February 1986. At the end of 2025, our Truckload Transportation Services ("TTS") segment had a fleet of 7,100 trucks, of which 6,785 were company-operated and 315 were owned and operated by independent contractors. Our Werner Logistics segment operated an additional 27 drayage company trucks and 170 Final Mile delivery trucks at the end of 2025. We have historically grown organically, and more recently through a combination of organic growth and business acquisitions (discussed below). Our business acquisitions expanded our fleet size, customer base, geographic market presence, and network of operational facilities. We remain open to considering acquisitions in North America truckload and logistics companies that are both additive to our business and accretive to our earnings.

We have two reportable segments – TTS and Werner Logistics. Our TTS segment is comprised of Dedicated and One-Way Truckload. Dedicated had 4,850 trucks as of December 31, 2025 and provides truckload services dedicated to a specific customer, generally for a retail distribution center or manufacturing facility, utilizing either dry van or specialized trailers. One-Way Truckload had 2,250 trucks as of December 31, 2025 and includes the following operating fleets: (i) the medium-to-long-haul van ("Van") fleet transports a variety of consumer nondurable products and other commodities in truckload quantities over irregular routes using dry van trailers, including Mexico cross-border routes; (ii) the expedited ("Expedited") fleet provides time-sensitive truckload services utilizing driver teams; (iii) the regional short-haul ("Regional") fleet provides comparable truckload van service within geographic regions across the United States; and (iv) the Temperature Controlled fleet provides truckload services for temperature sensitive products over irregular routes utilizing temperature-controlled trailers. Our TTS fleets operate throughout the 48 contiguous U.S. states pursuant to operating authority, both common and contract, granted by U.S. Department of Transportation ("DOT") and pursuant to intrastate authority granted by various U.S. states. We also have authority to operate in several provinces of Canada and to provide through-trailer service into and out of Mexico. The principal types of freight we transport include retail store merchandise, consumer products, food and beverage products and manufactured products. We focus on transporting consumer nondurable products that generally ship more consistently throughout the year and whose volumes are generally more stable during a slowdown in the economy.

Our Werner Logistics segment is a non-asset-based transportation and logistics provider. Werner Logistics provides services throughout North America and generates the majority of our non-trucking revenues through three divisions. These three Werner Logistics divisions are as follows: (i) Truckload Logistics, which uses contracted carriers to complete shipments for brokerage customers and freight management customers for which we offer a full range of single-source logistics management services and solutions; (ii) the intermodal ("Intermodal") unit offers rail transportation through alliances with rail and drayage providers as an alternative to truck transportation; and (iii) Werner Final Mile ("Final Mile") offers residential and commercial deliveries of large or heavy items using third-party agents, independent contractors, and Company employees with two-person delivery teams operating a liftgate straight truck.

On January 27, 2026, we acquired 100% of the equity interests in First Enterprises, Inc., doing business as FirstFleet, Inc. ("FirstFleet"). FirstFleet, based in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, is a dedicated truckload carrier that sustained profitable growth

over four decades and cultivated deep relationships with top-tier customers under multi-year contracts. Truckload revenues generated by FirstFleet will be reported in Dedicated within our TTS segment.

Our business philosophy is to provide superior on-time customer service at a significant value for our customers. To accomplish this, we operate premium modern tractors and trailers. This equipment has fewer mechanical and maintenance issues and helps attract and retain experienced drivers. We continually develop our business processes and technology to improve customer service and driver retention. We focus on customers who value the broad geographic coverage, diversified truck and logistics services, equipment capacity, technology, customized services and flexibility available from a large, financially-stable transportation and logistics provider.

We operate in the truckload and logistics sectors of the transportation industry. Our TTS segment provides specialized services to customers based on (i) each customer's trailer needs (such as van and temperature-controlled trailers), (ii) geographic area (regional and medium-to-long-haul van, including transport throughout Mexico and Canada), (iii) time-sensitive shipments (expedited) or (iv) conversion of their private fleet to us (dedicated). In 2025, TTS segment revenues accounted for 69% of total operating revenues, Werner Logistics revenues accounted for 29% of total operating revenues, and the remaining 2% was recorded in non-reportable segments. Our Werner Logistics segment manages the transportation and logistics requirements for customers, providing customers with additional sources of truck capacity, alternative modes of transportation, and systems analysis to optimize transportation needs. Werner Logistics services include (i) truck brokerage, (ii) freight management, (iii) intermodal transport, and (iv) final mile. Werner Logistics is highly dependent on qualified associates, information systems and the services of qualified third-party capacity providers. You can find the revenues generated by services that accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated revenues, consisting of TTS and Werner Logistics, for the last three years in Note 2 and Note 14 in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements under Item 8 of Part II of this Form 10-K.

We have a diversified freight base but are dependent on a relatively small number of customers for a significant portion of our revenues. During 2025, our largest 5, 10, 25 and 50 customers comprised 38%, 50%, 68% and 79% of our revenues, respectively. Our largest customer, Dollar General, accounted for 11% of our total revenues in 2025. Revenues generated by Dollar General are reported in both of our reportable operating segments. The industry groups of our top 50 customers are 66% retail and consumer products, 13% food and beverage, 13% manufacturing/industrial, and 8% logistics and other. Many of our One-Way Truckload customer contracts may be terminated upon 30 days' notice, which is common in the truckload industry. We have longer-term Dedicated customer contracts, most of which are two to five years in length (including some contracts with annual evergreen clauses) and generally may be terminated by either party typically upon a notice period following the expiration of the contract's first year. We typically renegotiate rates with our customers for these Dedicated contracts on an annual basis.

Our company and independent contractor tractors are equipped with communication devices. These devices enable us and our drivers to conduct two-way communication using standardized and freeform messages. This technology also allows us to plan and monitor shipment progress. We automatically monitor truck movement and obtain specific data on the location of trucks at fixed intervals. Using the real-time global positioning data obtained from the devices, we have advanced application systems to improve customer and driver service. We were the first trucking company in the United States to receive an exemption from DOT to use a global positioning-based paperless log system as an alternative to the paper logbooks traditionally used by truck drivers to track their daily work activities. Since January 2021, we have used an untethered, tablet-based telematics solution that provides an enhanced and more efficient driver experience.

Safety is a high priority for us, which is demonstrated through our continued safety investments and initiatives, such as investing in equipment with the latest collision mitigation systems; leveraging side-view camera technology; implementing in-cab and desktop technologies aimed at improving weather alerts; rerouting, and other situational awareness for our professional drivers and transportation management teams. Improved weather reporting aids in redirecting our professional drivers to safer routes, together with our other safety initiatives, may decrease claims and costs associated with claims.

In the trucking industry, revenues generally follow a seasonal pattern. Peak freight demand has historically occurred in the months of September, October and November. After the December holiday season and during the remaining winter months, our freight volumes are typically lower because some customers reduce shipment levels. Our operating expenses have historically been higher in the winter months due primarily to decreased fuel efficiency, increased cold weather-related maintenance costs of revenue equipment and increased insurance and claims costs attributed to adverse winter weather conditions. We attempt to minimize the impact of seasonality through our marketing program by seeking additional freight from certain customers during traditionally slower shipping periods and focusing on transporting consumer nondurable products. Revenue can also be affected
by adverse weather conditions, holidays and the number of business days that occur during a given period because revenue is directly related to the available working days of shippers.

Employee Count: As of December 31, 2025, we employed 8,677 drivers; 638 mechanics and maintenance associates for the trucking operation; 1,465 office associates for the trucking operation; and 1,251 associates for Werner Logistics, international, driving schools and other non-trucking operations. Most of our associates are based in the U.S., with about 1% based in Mexico and Canada. None of our U.S. or Canadian associates are represented by a collective bargaining unit, and we generally consider relations with our associates to be good.

Health & Safety: Werner® fosters a robust safety culture focused on minimizing workplace incidents, risks, and hazards. In 2025, Werner continued to achieve reductions in workplace injuries and DOT preventable accidents per million miles. The Werner Safety Department oversees compliance and training for drivers under DOT regulations and Company policies. Key responsibilities include creating and delivering world-class training programs on driver certification, driver onboarding and testing, hazardous materials handling, and anti-human trafficking training. Our strong safety culture is demonstrated by ongoing investments in advanced equipment technologies, which lead to improved safety for our professional drivers. Nearly all of our company-owned trucks have collision-mitigation safety systems, automated manual transmissions, and forward-facing cameras.

headings: Risks Related to our Business and Industry
Our business is subject to overall economic and geopolitical conditions that could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.
Increases in fuel prices and shortages of fuel can have a material adverse effect on the results of operations and profitability.
We operate in a highly competitive industry, which may limit growth opportunities and reduce profitability.
The seasonal shipping pattern generally experienced in the trucking industry may affect our periodic results during traditional slower shipping periods and winter months.
We depend on key customers, the loss or financial failure of which may have a material adverse effect on our operations and profitability.
We depend on the services of third-party capacity providers, the availability of which could affect our profitability and limit growth in our Werner Logistics segment.
If we cannot effectively manage the challenges associated with doing business internationally, our revenues and profitability may suffer.
We rely on the services of key personnel, the loss of which could impact our future success.
Difficulty in obtaining, or increased costs of, materials, equipment, goods, and services from our vendors and suppliers could adversely affect our business.
A public health crisis, such as an epidemic, pandemic, or similar outbreak may have an adverse impact on our business, as well as the operations of our customers and suppliers.
Risks Related to Legal, Regulatory and Environmental, Social and Governance ("ESG") Matters
Scrutiny from investors and other stakeholders regarding ESG related matters may have a negative impact on our business.
Risks Related to Financial Matters
Our earnings could be reduced by increases in the number of insurance claims, cost per claim, costs of insurance premiums, availability of insurance coverage, or a significant uninsured liability.
Decreased demand for our used revenue equipment could result in lower unit sales and resale values.
paragraphs: The following risks and uncertainties may cause our actual results, business, financial condition and cash flows to materially differ from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements included in this Form 10-K. Caution should be taken not to place undue reliance on forward-looking statements made herein because such statements speak only to the date they were made. Unless otherwise required by applicable securities laws, we undertake no obligation or duty to revise or update any forward-looking statements contained herein to reflect subsequent events or circumstances or the occurrence of unanticipated events. Also refer to the Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements in Item 7 of Part II of this Form 10-K.

We are sensitive to economic or geopolitical conditions, in particular, those that impact customer shipping volumes, industry freight demand, and industry truck capacity. Such conditions can include, among others, employment levels, business conditions, fuel and energy costs, public health crises, interest rates, tax rates, political conflict, and global trade policy. Tariffs or trade regulations may impact the cost or availability of materials, equipment, goods, and fuel. On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the U.S. government cannot use the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to impose tariffs, overturning certain recent tariffs announced throughout 2025, including those on global imports from China, Canada and Mexico. This decision creates uncertainty about the immediate path forward for many supply chains. Not all tariffs announced throughout 2025 will be impacted by this U.S. Supreme Court decision since many tariffs were imposed under other legal authorities that remain in effect and new tariffs may continue to be implemented through these other legal authorities. Impacts from any of the foregoing on (i) our suppliers could affect pricing or availability of needed goods and services and (ii) our customers could weaken their financial condition, increase our risk of bad debt losses, and decrease demand for our services (even if preceded by increased demand in anticipation of a trade regulation or other change). When conditions cause a decline in shipping volumes or an increase in available truck capacity, freight pricing generally becomes more competitive as carriers compete for loads to maintain truck productivity. Any of the foregoing may impact our results of operations and financial condition.

Labor and employment matters, including difficulty in recruiting and retaining experienced drivers, recent driver training school graduates and independent contractors, could impact our results of operations and financial condition.

At times, the trucking industry has experienced driver shortages. Driver turnover, recruiting and availability may be affected by changes in our customer base, fleet size, and workforce demographics; alternative employment opportunities and national unemployment rates; freight market conditions; availability of financial aid for driver training schools; and changing industry regulations. If such a shortage were to occur and driver pay rate increases became necessary to attract and retain drivers, our results of operations would be negatively impacted to the extent that we could not obtain corresponding freight rate increases. Additionally, a shortage of drivers could result in idled equipment, which would affect our profitability and limit growth opportunities.

The impact on independent contractors of inflationary cost increases and the market for and cost of financing equipment may affect their availability to us. In recent years, the classification of individuals as employees or independent contractors has gained increased attention among tax and other regulators, as well as plaintiffs' attorneys who have pursued lawsuits against transportation companies alleging misclassification of employees and independent contractors resulting in significant damages. Changes that impact the classification of the relationship between us and our independent contractors could have a material adverse effect on our ability to recruit and retain them, which could negatively impact our operations. If pay rates for drivers or per-mile settlement rates for independent contractors increased, our results of operations would be negatively impacted to the extent that we could not obtain corresponding freight rate increases.

During 2023, union organizing efforts occurred at two locations of a U.S. subsidiary, which resulted in fewer than 30 of our employees being represented by a union. In September 2024, that small group of drivers filed a petition seeking to decertify the union and end their union's representation. The union responded by voluntarily ending its representation of those drivers and, as a result, those drivers are no longer unionized. Unionization, if broad-based, could have a material adverse effect on our costs, efficiency, and profitability.

paragraphs: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") summarizes the financial statements from management's perspective with respect to our financial condition, results of operations, liquidity and other factors that may affect actual results. The MD&A is organized in the following sections:
•Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements •Overview •Results of Operations •Liquidity and Capital Resources

This Annual Report on Form 10-K contains historical information and forward-looking statements based on information currently available to our management. The forward-looking statements in this report, including those made in this Item 7 (Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations), are made pursuant to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, as amended. These safe harbor provisions encourage reporting companies to provide prospective information to investors. Forward-looking statements can be identified by the use of certain words, such as "anticipate," "believe," "estimate," "expect," "intend," "plan," "project," and other similar terms and language. We believe the forward-looking statements are reasonable based on currently available information. However, forward-looking statements involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions, whether known or unknown, that could cause our actual results, business, financial condition and cash flows to differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements. A discussion of important factors relating to forward-looking statements is included in Item 1A (Risk Factors) of Part I of this Form 10-K. Readers should not unduly rely on the forward-looking statements included in this Form 10-K because such statements speak only to the date they were made. Unless otherwise required by applicable securities laws, we undertake no obligation or duty to update or revise any forward-looking statements contained herein to reflect subsequent events or circumstances or the occurrence of unanticipated events.

We have two reportable segments, TTS and Werner Logistics, and we operate in the truckload and logistics sectors of the transportation industry. In the truckload sector, we focus on transporting consumer nondurable products that generally ship more consistently throughout the year. In the logistics sector, besides managing transportation requirements for individual customers, we provide additional sources of truck capacity, alternative modes of transportation, a North American delivery network and systems analysis to optimize transportation needs. Our success depends on our ability to efficiently and effectively manage our resources in the delivery of truckload transportation and logistics services to our customers. Resource requirements vary with customer demand, which may be subject to seasonal or general economic conditions. Our ability to adapt to changes in customer transportation requirements is essential to efficiently deploy resources and make capital investments in tractors and trailers (with respect to our TTS segment) or obtain qualified third-party capacity at a reasonable price (with respect to our Werner Logistics segment). We may also be affected by our customers' financial failures or loss of customer business.

Revenues for the operating segments (Dedicated and One-Way Truckload) within our TTS reportable segment are typically generated on a per-mile basis and also include revenues such as stop charges, loading and unloading charges, equipment detention charges and equipment repositioning charges. To mitigate our risk to fuel price increases, we recover additional fuel surcharge revenues from our customers that generally recoup a majority of the increased fuel costs; however, we cannot assure that current recovery levels will continue in future periods. Because fuel surcharge revenues fluctuate in response to changes in fuel costs, we identify them separately and exclude them from the statistical calculations to provide a more meaningful comparison between periods. The key statistics used to evaluate trucking revenues, net of fuel surcharge, are (i) average revenues per tractor per week, (ii) One-Way Truckload average revenues per total mile, (iii) average percentage of empty miles (miles without trailer cargo), (iv) average trip length (in loaded miles) and (v) average number of tractors in service. General economic conditions, seasonal trucking industry freight patterns and industry capacity are important factors that impact these statistics. Our TTS segment also generates a small amount of revenues categorized as non-trucking revenues, which consist primarily of the intra-Mexico portion of cross-border shipments delivered to or from Mexico where the TTS segment utilizes a third-party capacity provider. We exclude such revenues from the statistical calculations.

Our most significant resource requirements are company drivers, independent contractors, tractors, and trailers with respect to our TTS segment and qualified third-party capacity providers with respect to our Werner Logistics segment. Independent contractors supply their own tractors and drivers and are responsible for their operating expenses. Our financial results are affected by company driver and independent contractor availability and the markets for new and used revenue equipment. We are self-insured for a significant portion of bodily injury, property damage and cargo claims; workers' compensation claims; and associate health claims (supplemented by premium-based insurance coverage above certain dollar levels). For that reason, our financial results may also be affected by driver safety, medical costs, weather, legal and regulatory environments and insurance coverage costs to protect against catastrophic losses.

The operating ratio is a common industry measure used to evaluate our profitability and that of our TTS segment operating fleets. The operating ratio consists of operating expenses expressed as a percentage of operating revenues. The most significant variable expenses that impact the TTS segment are driver salaries and benefits, fuel, fuel taxes (included in taxes and licenses expense), payments to independent contractors (included in rent and purchased transportation expense), supplies and maintenance and insurance and claims. As discussed further in the comparison of operating results for 2025 to 2024, several industry-wide issues have caused, and could continue to cause, costs to increase in future periods. These issues include shortages of drivers or independent contractors, changing fuel prices, changing used truck and trailer pricing, compliance with new or proposed regulations and tightening of the commercial truck liability insurance market. Our main fixed costs include depreciation expense for tractors and trailers and non-driver salaries, wages and benefits. The TTS segment requires substantial cash expenditures for tractor and trailer purchases. We fund these purchases with net cash from operations and financing available under our existing credit facilities, as management deems necessary.

We provide non-trucking services primarily through the three divisions within our Werner Logistics segment (Truckload Logistics, Intermodal, and Final Mile). Unlike our TTS segment, the Werner Logistics segment is less asset-intensive and is instead dependent upon qualified associates, information systems and qualified third-party capacity providers. The largest expense item related to the Werner Logistics segment is the cost of purchased transportation we pay to third-party capacity providers. This expense item is recorded as rent and purchased transportation expense. Other operating expenses consist primarily of salaries, wages and benefits, as well as depreciation and amortization, supplies and maintenance, and other general expenses. We evaluate the Werner Logistics segment's financial performance by reviewing operating expenses and operating income expressed as a percentage of revenues. Purchased transportation expenses as a percentage of revenues can be impacted by the rates charged to customers and the costs of securing third-party capacity. We have a mix of contracted long-term rates and variable rates for the cost of third-party capacity, and we cannot assure that our operating results will not be adversely impacted in the future if our ability to obtain qualified third-party capacity providers changes or the rates of such providers increase.

At the end of 2025, we believe we are well positioned with a strong balance sheet and sufficient liquidity. Our debt is at $752 million, or a net debt ratio (debt less cash) of 2.0 times earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, and restructuring and impairment for the year ended December 31, 2025. We had available liquidity of $702 million, considering cash and cash equivalents on hand and available borrowing capacity of $642 million. As of December 31, 2025, we were in compliance with our debt covenants and expect to continue to be in compliance in 2026. We currently plan to continue paying our quarterly dividend, which we have paid quarterly since 1987. This cash outlay currently results in approximately $8.4 million per quarter. Net capital expenditures (primarily revenue equipment) in 2026 currently are expected to be in the range of $185 million to $225 million.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家運輸與物流公司，主要從事跨州與州內運輸一般商品的貨櫃運輸業務。本公司亦透過 Werner Logistics 分部提供物流服務。本公司認為我們是美國最大的貨櫃運輸業者之一（以總營運收入為準），本公司總部設於內布拉斯加州奧馬哈市，位於本公司貨櫃運輸服務區域的地理中心。本公司於 1956 年由 Clarence L. Werner 資助創立，當時他年僅 19 歲，僅以一輛貨車開始業務。本公司於 1982 年 9 月在內布拉斯加州註冊成立，並於 1986 年 6 月完成首次公開發行，當時本公司擁有 632 輛貨車，截至 1986 年 2 月。截至 2025 年年底，本公司 Truckload Transportation Services（"TTS"）分部擁有 7,100 輛貨車，其中 6,785 輛為本公司自行運營，315 輛為獨立承包商所有並運營。本公司 Werner Logistics 分部於 2025 年年底運營額外 27 輛拖車公司貨車與 170 輛 Final Mile 配送貨車。本公司歷來以內生成長為主，近期則透過內生成長與企業併購（以下將討論）進行擴張。本公司企業併購擴大了本公司貨車規模、客戶羣、地理市場存在與營運設施網路。本公司仍對考慮在北美貨櫃與物流公司進行併購，這些公司對本公司業務具有加值性，且對本公司獲利具有正面影響。

本公司有兩個應報告分部 – TTS 與 Werner Logistics。本公司 TTS 分部包含 Dedicated 與 One-Way Truckload。Dedicated 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日擁有 4,850 輛貨車，提供專屬特定客戶的貨櫃運輸服務，通常為零售分銷中心或製造廠，使用乾式貨櫃或專用拖車。One-Way Truckload 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日擁有 2,250 輛貨車，包含以下營運貨車隊：(i) 中至長途貨櫃（"Van"）貨車隊運輸多種消費性非耐用品及其他商品，以貨櫃數量運輸，沿不規則路線運送，使用乾式貨櫃拖車，包括墨西哥跨境路線；(ii) 加速（"Expedited"）貨車隊提供時間敏感的貨櫃運輸服務，使用駕駛團隊；(iii) 地區短途（"Regional"）貨車隊提供美國各地理區域內的貨櫃運輸服務；(iv) 溫度控制貨車隊提供溫度敏感商品的貨櫃運輸服務，沿不規則路線運送，使用溫度控制拖車。本公司 TTS 貨車隊根據美國運輸部（"DOT"）授予的運營權限，包括普通與合同運營權限，以及各美國州政府授予的州內運營權限，運營於美國 48 個連續州。本公司亦有權在加拿大數個省份運營，並提供透過拖車服務進入與離開墨西哥。本公司主要運輸的貨物包括零售商店商品、消費性產品、食品與飲料產品及製造產品。本公司專注於運輸消費性非耐用品，這些產品通常全年運輸較為穩定，且在經濟放緩時，其運輸量通常較為穩定。

本公司 Werner Logistics 分部為一家非資產型的運輸與物流服務提供者。Werner Logistics 在北美提供服務，並透過三個部門產生本公司非貨櫃運輸收入的絕大部分。這三個 Werner Logistics 部門如下：(i) 貨櫃物流，使用合約運輸業者完成經紀客戶與貨運管理客戶的運輸，本公司為這些客戶提供完整的單一來源物流管理服務與解決方案；(ii) 聯運（"Intermodal"）部門透過與鐵路與拖車運輸業者的合作，提供鐵路運輸服務，作為貨櫃運輸的替代方案；(iii) Werner Final Mile（"Final Mile"）提供住宅與商業的大型或重型物品配送服務，使用第三方代理、獨立承包商與本公司員工，以兩人配送團隊操作升降貨叉貨車。
本公司於 2026 年 1 月 27 日取得 First Enterprises, Inc.（經營業務為 FirstFleet, Inc.（"FirstFleet"））100% 的股權。FirstFleet 位於田納西州默弗里斯伯勒，為一家專屬貨櫃運輸業者，持續實現獲利成長，已維持四十年的穩定成長，並與頂級客戶建立深厚關係，透過多年合約。
FirstFleet 產生的貨櫃收入將計入本公司 TTS 分部的 Dedicated 項目。
本公司業務哲學為為客戶提供優質準時的客戶服務，並以顯著價值服務客戶。為達成此目標，本公司運營高品質現代的牽引車與拖車。此設備機械與維護問題較少，有助於吸引與留住經驗豐富的駕駛員。本公司持續發展業務流程與科技，以提升客戶服務與駕駛員留存率。本公司專注於重視廣泛地理覆蓋、多樣化貨櫃與物流服務、設備容量、科技、客製化服務與靈活性的客戶，這些服務來自一家規模大、財務穩定的運輸與物流服務提供者。

本公司運營於運輸業的貨櫃與物流部門。本公司 TTS 分部根據 (i) 每個客戶的拖車需求（如貨櫃與溫度控制拖車），(ii) 地理區域（區域與中至長途貨櫃，包括運送至墨西哥與加拿大），(iii) 時間敏感貨運（加速）或 (iv) 將其私有貨車隊轉交我們（專屬）為客戶提供專門服務。2025 年，TTS 分部收入佔總營運收入的 69%，Werner Logistics 收入佔總營運收入的 29%，剩餘 2% 記錄於非應報告分部。本公司 Werner Logistics 分部管理客戶的運輸與物流需求，為客戶提供額外的貨車容量、替代運輸方式與系統分析，以優化運輸需求。Werner Logistics 服務包括 (i) 貨櫃經紀，(ii) 貨運管理，(iii) 聯運運輸，以及 (iv) 最後一公里。Werner Logistics 高度依賴合格員工、資訊系統與合格第三方運力提供者。您可在本 Form 10-K 第二部分第 8 項「財務會計資訊」附註 2 與附註 14 中找到過去三年中，佔本公司合併收入 10% 以上之服務收入，包含 TTS 與 Werner Logistics 的收入。

本公司擁有多元化的貨運基礎，但對少數客戶的收入依賴程度較高。2025 年，本公司前五大、十大、二十五大與五十大客戶佔收入比例分別為 38%、50%、68% 與 79%。本公司最大客戶 Dollar General 在 2025 年佔本公司總收入的 11%。Dollar General 產生的收入同時計入本公司兩個應報告營運分部。本公司前五十大客戶的產業類別為 66% 零售與消費性產品、13% 食品與飲料、13% 製造與工業，以及 8% 物流與其他。許多本公司 One-Way Truckload 客戶合約可在 30 天通知期內終止，這在貨櫃運輸業中為常見做法。本公司擁有較長的 Dedicated 客戶合約，大多數合約為兩至五年（包括部分合約包含年度自動續約條款），通常在合約第一年到期後，任一方均可透過通知期終止合約。本公司通常每年與客戶重新協議這些 Dedicated 合約的費用。

本公司與獨立承包商所使用的牽引車均裝備有通訊裝置。這些裝置使本公司與駕駛員能夠透過標準化及自由格式訊息進行雙向通訊。此技術也使本公司能夠規劃並監測貨運進度。我們自動監測貨車行進狀況，並在固定間隔取得貨車位置的特定資料。利用從裝置中取得的即時全球定位資料，我們擁有先進的應用系統以提升客戶與駕駛員的服務品質。本公司是美國第一家獲得美國運輸部（DOT）免除，得以使用基於全球定位系統的無紙化日誌系統，作為取代傳統由貨車駕駛員用來追蹤每日工作活動的紙本日誌系統的運輸公司。自2021年1月起，本公司已使用一種無線連接、基於平板電腦的遠端資訊系統，提供更優化且更高效的駕駛員體驗。
安全對本公司而言是首要考量，這一點透過我們持續的安全投資與措施可見一斑，例如投資具備最新防撞系統的設備；運用側視鏡攝影機技術；實行車內與桌面技術，以提升天氣警報；重新導航，以及其它情境感知功能，以提升專業駕駛員與運輸管理團隊的安全性。改善的天氣報告有助於將專業駕駛員導向更安全的路線，加上我們的其他安全措施，可能降低與聲請賠償相關的聲請與成本。

在貨運業中，營收通常呈現季節性模式。歷史上的高峯貨運需求多發生在9月、10月與11月。在聖誕節假期過後，以及冬季剩餘月份，我們的貨運量通常較低，因為部分客戶會減少貨運量。我們的營運費用在冬季月份通常較高，主要原因是燃料效率降低、收入設備因寒冷天氣相關的維護成本增加，以及因惡劣冬季天氣條件導致的保險與聲請賠償成本增加。我們透過行銷方案來試圖降低季節性影響，於傳統上較為緩慢的貨運時期，尋求來自特定客戶的額外貨運，並專注於運輸消費性非耐用品。
營收也可能受到惡劣天氣條件、節日以及特定期間內的營業日數量的影響，因為營收與發貨商的可用工作日數直接相關。
員工人數：截至2025年12月31日，本公司僱用了8,677名駕駛員；638名機械與維護助理，用於貨運運作；1,465名辦公室助理，用於貨運運作；以及1,251名助理，用於 Werner Logistics、國際業務、駕駛學校及其他非貨運運作。本公司大多數員工位於美國，約有1%位於墨西哥與加拿大。我們的美國或加拿大員工均未加入集體談判單位，我們通常認為與員工的關係良好。

健康與安全：Werner® 培養強大的安全文化，專注於降低工作場所的事故、風險與危害。在2025年，Werner 繼續實現每百萬英里工作場所傷害與 DOT 可預防事故的減少。Werner 安全部門監督駕駛員在 DOT 規範與公司政策下的合規與培訓。主要責任包括建立並提供世界級的駕駛員認證、駕駛員入職與測試、危險品處理以及反人口販運培訓。我們強大的安全文化透過持續投資先進的設備技術，以提升專業駕駛員的安全性而體現。我們公司所有的貨車中，幾乎全部都裝備有防撞系統、自動變速器與前向攝影機。

paragraphs: 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析（"MD&A"）從管理層的觀點總結財務報表，關於我們的財務狀況、營運成果、流動性及其他可能影響實際結果的因素。MD&A 的組織結構如下：
• 警示有關未來展望聲明之注意事項 • 總覽 • 營運成果 • 流動性與資本資源

本年度10-K表報文件包含歷史資訊與未來展望聲明，基於目前管理層可取得之資訊。本報告中之未來展望聲明（包括本項目7（管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析）所作之聲明）係根據1995年私人證券訴訟改革法案（Private Securities Litigation Reform Act）之安全港條款所作出。這些安全港條款鼓勵報告公司向投資者提供前瞻性資訊。未來展望聲明可透過使用某些特定詞彙加以辨識，例如 "預期"、"相信"、"估計"、"預期"、"意圖"、"計畫"、"預測" 以及其他相似的詞彙與語言。我們認為這些未來展望聲明是基於目前可取得資訊所作出的合理聲明。然而，未來展望聲明涉及風險、不確定性與假設，無論是否已知，這些因素都可能導致我們的實際結果、業務、財務狀況與現金流與未來展望聲明所預期的有重大差異。有關未來展望聲明的重要因素討論，請參閱本10-K表報文件第一部分第1A項（風險因素）。讀者不應過度依賴本10-K表報文件中所包含的未來展望聲明，因為這些聲明僅針對其作出之日期而言。除非適用證券法另有規定，否則我們不承擔更新或修正任何 herein 所包含之未來展望聲明以反映後續事件或情況或未預期事件之義務或責任。

我們有兩個應報告分部，TTS 以及 Werner Logistics，我們經營於運輸業的貨車載重與物流部門。在貨車載重部門，我們專注於運輸消費者非耐用品，這些產品通常全年運輸較為穩定。在物流部門，除了管理個別客戶的運輸需求外，我們還提供額外的貨車容量、替代運輸方式、北美配送網路與系統分析以優化運輸需求。我們的成功取決於我們能否有效地管理資源，以提供貨車載重運輸與物流服務給客戶。資源需求會隨著客戶需求而變化，而客戶需求可能受到季節性或總體經濟條件的影響。我們適應客戶運輸需求變化的能力建立於有效部署資源與進行貨車與拖車（針對TTS分部）或取得合資格的第三方容量（針對Werner Logistics分部）的資本投資上。我們也可能受到客戶財務失敗或失去客戶業務的影響。

TTS應報告分部內的營運分部（專屬與單程貨車載重）之營收通常以每英里為單位產生，並包括停車費、裝卸費、設備停置費與設備重新定位費等收入。為降低燃料價格上漲的風險，我們從客戶處收取額外的燃料附加費收入，通常可回收大部分增加的燃料成本；然而，我們無法保證目前的回收水平會在未來期間持續。由於燃料附加費收入會根據燃料成本的變化而波動，我們會將其單獨識別並排除於統計計算中，以提供更有意義的期間比較。用來評估貨車運輸收入（扣除燃料附加費）的關鍵統計資料為（i）每輛貨車每週平均收入、（ii）單程貨車載重每總英里平均收入、（iii）平均空英里比例（無拖車貨物的英里數）、（iv）平均行程長度（載貨英里數）以及（v）平均在役貨車數量。總體經濟條件、季節性貨車運輸業貨物運輸模式與產業容量是影響這些統計資料的重要因素。我們的TTS分部也產生少量被歸類為非貨車運輸收入的收入，這些收入主要由墨西哥境內跨境運輸的墨西哥部分組成，這些運輸由TTS分部使用第三方容量供應商進行。我們會將這些收入排除於統計計算中。

我們最重要的資源需求為公司駕駛員、獨立承包商、貨車與拖車（針對TTS分部）以及合資格的第三方容量供應商（針對Werner Logistics分部）。獨立承包商提供自己的貨車與駕駛員，並承擔其營運費用。我們的財務結果會受到公司駕駛員與獨立承包商的可得性以及新舊運輸設備市場的影響。我們對大部分身體傷害、財產損壞與貨物聲請、員工補償聲請以及員工健康聲請（超過特定金額水平時補充以基於保費的保險覆蓋）自負風險；因此，我們的財務結果也可能受到駕駛員安全、醫療費用、天氣、法律與法規環境以及保險覆蓋費用的影響，以保護對抗重大損失。

運營比率是業界常用的指標，用以評估我們的利潤率以及TTS分部運營車隊的利潤率。運營比率由運營費用表示為運營收入的百分比組成。影響TTS分部的最主要變動費用為駕駛員薪資與福利、燃料、燃料稅（包含在稅務與執照費用中）、支付給獨立承包商的費用（包含在租金與購買運輸費用中）、物料與維護費用以及保險與聲請費用。如進一步比較2025年與2024年的運營結果所述，幾個產業範圍內的問題已導致，並可能繼續導致未來期間的費用增加。這些問題包括駕駛員或獨立承包商的短缺、燃料價格的變化、二手貨車與拖車價格的變化、符合新或擬議的法規以及商業貨車責任保險市場的緊縮。我們的主要固定費用包括貨車與拖車的折舊費用以及非駕駛員薪資、工資與福利。TTS分部需要大量現金支出用於貨車與拖車的購買。我們透過營運活動產生的淨現金與現有信貸設施下的融資資金來資助這些購買，如管理層認為必要。

我們主要透過Werner Logistics分部內的三個部門（貨車載重物流、多式運輸與最後一哩）提供非貨車運輸服務。與我們的TTS分部不同，Werner Logistics分部較少依賴資產，而是依賴合格員工、資訊系統與合格第三方容量供應商。與Werner Logistics分部相關的最主要費用項目為我們支付給第三方容量供應商的購運費用。此費用項目被記錄為租金與購運費用。其他運營費用主要由薪資、工資與福利費用，以及折舊與攤銷、物料與維護費用，以及其他一般費用組成。我們透過評估運營費用與運營收入表示為收入的百分比來評估Werner Logistics分部的財務表現。購運費用表示為收入的百分比可能受到客戶收取費用率與取得第三方容量費用的影響。我們有不同類型的長期合約費用率與變動費用率來計算第三方容量費用，我們無法保證如果我們取得合格第三方容量供應商的能力改變或這些供應商的費用率上升，我們的運營結果不會在未來受到不利影響。

於 2025 年底，我們認為本公司擁有強固的資產負債表與充足的流動性，處於優勢地位。本公司負債為 752 百萬美元，淨負債比率（負債減現金）為 2.0 倍營業收入前利息、所得稅、折舊及攤銷，以及重組及減損費用，於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度。本公司可運用流動性為 702 百萬美元，考量現金及現金等價物與可運用借款能力為 642 百萬美元。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司符合本公司負債契約條件，預期於 2026 年持續符合。本公司目前計畫持續發放每季股息，自 1987 年以來已持續每季發放。此現金支出目前約為每季 8.4 百萬美元。2026 年淨資本支出（主要為收入設備）目前預期為 185 百萬至 225 百萬美元之間。

headings: 與本公司業務及產業相關之風險
本公司業務受總體經濟及地緣政治條件影響，可能對本公司營運結果及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
燃料價格上漲及燃料短缺可能對本公司營運結果及獲利能力造成重大不利影響。
本公司所處產業為高度競爭產業，可能限制成長機會並降低獲利能力。
貨車運輸產業一般所經驗之季節性運輸模式，可能在傳統運輸較慢時期及冬季月份影響本公司之週期性營運結果。
本公司依賴關鍵客戶，若該等客戶發生虧損或財務失敗，可能對本公司營運及獲利能力造成重大不利影響。
本公司依賴第三方容量供應商之服務，該等服務之可得性可能影響本公司獲利能力，並限制本公司 Werner Logistics 分部之成長。
若本公司無法有效管理國際業務相關之挑戰，本公司營收及獲利能力可能受影響。
我們依賴關鍵人員的服務，其流失可能影響我們未來的成功。
難以取得，或取得成本增加，來自我們供應商與經銷商的材料、設備、商品及服務，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
公共衛生危機，例如疫情、大流行或類似爆發，可能對我們的業務，以及我們客戶與供應商的運作產生不利影響。
與法律、法規及環境、社會和治理（"ESG"）事項相關的風險
投資者及其他利害關係人對ESG相關事項的關注，可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
與財務事項相關的風險
我們的獲利可能因保險理賠數量增加、每件理賠成本、保險 premiums 成本、保險覆蓋範圍的可取得性，或重大未投保責任而減少。
我們用過的收入設備需求減少，可能導致單位銷售數量與再售價值降低。
paragraphs: 下列風險與不確定性可能導致本公司實際結果、業務、財務狀況與現金流與本10-K表格所包含之預測性陳述有重大差異。應謹慎避免過度依賴 herein 所述之預測性陳述，因為這些陳述僅反映其做出之日期。除非適用之證券法另有要求，本公司不承擔任何義務或責任，以修正或更新 herein 所含之預測性陳述，以反映後續事件或情況或未預見事件之發生。另請參閱本10-K表格第二部分第七項之預測性陳述警示說明。

本公司對經濟或地緣政治條件敏感，特別是那些影響客戶貨運量、行業運輸需求與行業貨車容量之條件。這些條件可能包括，但不僅限於，就業水平、商業條件、燃料與能源成本、公共衛生危機、利率、稅率、政治衝突與全球貿易政策。關稅或貿易規範可能影響材料、設備、商品與燃料之成本或可得性。2026年2月20日，美國最高法院裁定美國政府無法使用國際緊急經濟權力法來課徵關稅，推翻了2025年所宣佈的某些關稅，包括針對來自中國、加拿大與墨西哥之全球進口商品之關稅。此裁決使許多供應鏈的即時發展路徑產生不確定性。2025年所宣佈的關稅並非全部會受到此美國最高法院裁決影響，因為許多關稅是根據其他法律權限所課徵，且這些法律權限仍然有效，未來可能繼續透過這些其他法律權限實施新關稅。上述任何影響可能導致(i)我方供應商之成本或所需商品與服務之可得性有所變動，以及(ii)我方客戶之財務狀況惡化，增加我方壞帳損失風險，並降低我方服務之需求（即使此需求是因貿易規範或其他變動而預期增加）。當條件導致貨運量下降或可用貨車容量增加時，運輸價格通常會變得更具競爭力，因為電信業者為維持貨車生產力而爭取貨載。上述任何情況都可能影響我方營運結果與財務狀況。
勞動與就業相關事項，包括招募與留住經驗豐富司機、近期司機訓練學校畢業生與獨立承包商之困難，可能影響我方營運結果與財務狀況。
有時，貨運業曾經歷司機短缺。司機流動率、招募與可得性可能受我方客戶羣體、車隊規模與勞工人口結構；替代性就業機會與全國失業率；貨運市場條件；司機訓練學校財務補助可得性；以及產業規範變動等因素影響。若發生司機短缺，且必須提高司機薪資以吸引與留住司機，則我方營運結果將受到負面影響，前提是我們無法取得相應的貨運價格上漲。此外，司機短缺可能導致設備閒置，這將影響我方利潤率並限制成長機會。

通貨膨脹成本上漲對獨立承包商之影響，以及設備市場與設備融資成本，可能影響其對我方之可得性。近年來，個人被歸類為員工或獨立承包商之問題，已引起稅務及其他監管機構，以及原告律師的更多關注，這些律師已對運輸公司提出訴訟，指控其誤將員工與獨立承包商歸類，導致重大損害。影響我方與獨立承包商之間關係歸類之變動，可能對我方招募與留住他們的能力產生重大負面影響，這可能對我方營運造成負面影響。若司機薪資或獨立承包商每英里結算率提高，我方營運結果將受到負面影響，前提是我們無法取得相應的貨運價格上漲。
2023年，美國子公司之兩處發生罷工組織活動，導致少於30名我方員工被工會代表。2024年9月，該小組司機提出請願，要求取消工會認證並終止工會之代表。工會隨即自願終止對這些司機之代表，因此這些司機已不再屬於工會。若工會化廣泛發生，可能對我方成本、效率與利潤率產生重大負面影響。
